questions.text: जल के विद्युत अपघटन में इलेक्ट्रोडों पर मुक्त हाइड्रोजन और ऑक्सीजन गैसों के द्रव्यमानों का अनुपात होता है:
questions.text_english: In the electrolysis of water, the mass ratio of hydrogen and oxygen gases liberated at the electrodes is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) 1 : 8. In the electrolysis of water (2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂), two moles of hydrogen gas and one mole of oxygen gas are produced. The molar mass of H₂ is 2 g/mol and that of O₂ is 32 g/mol. So mass of H₂ = 2 × 2 = 4 g and mass of O₂ = 1 × 32 = 32 g. The ratio is 4 : 32 = 1 : 8. Options A and B are incorrect as they confuse mole ratio with mass ratio. Option D (1:16) is also incorrect as it over-estimates oxygen's mass.
questions.solution_hindi: जल के विद्युत अपघटन में 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂ अभिक्रिया होती है। H₂ का द्रव्यमान = 4 g और O₂ का द्रव्यमान = 32 g। अतः अनुपात = 4:32 = 1:8।

questions.text: मानव शरीर के कार्य करने के pH का परास (परिसर) है:
questions.text_english: The body of human beings works within the pH range of:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) 7.0 to 7.8. The human body maintains a slightly alkaline internal environment with a pH range of 7.0 to 7.8. Blood pH is maintained between 7.35 and 7.45. Options A and B suggest acidic ranges which are incompatible with normal body function. Option D (7.5 to 8.1) is too high. Any significant deviation from the 7.0–7.8 range can lead to serious health complications.
questions.solution_hindi: मानव शरीर की कार्यशील अवस्था में pH का परास 7.0 से 7.8 होता है। रक्त का pH 7.35 से 7.45 के बीच रहता है जो शरीर की आंतरिक क्षारीय प्रकृति को दर्शाता है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किसके हाइड्रॉक्साइड से भरे बर्तनों (पात्रों) पर दिए गए आरेख में दर्शाया गया चेतावनी चिह्न आवश्यक रूप से लगाया जाना चाहिए?
questions.text_english: The warning sign shown in the given figure must invariably be displayed/pasted on the containers which contain hydroxide of:
questions.image_description: A triangular warning sign (corrosive hazard symbol) showing liquid dripping from a surface onto a hand, indicating a corrosive substance. The sign has a red border and yellow background.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Sodium. The warning sign shown is the corrosive hazard symbol. Sodium hydroxide (NaOH), also known as caustic soda, is a highly corrosive and caustic substance that can cause severe burns to skin and eyes. Aluminium hydroxide and Magnesium hydroxide are mild bases used even in medicines, while Calcium hydroxide (lime water) is also relatively mild. Only Sodium hydroxide is strongly corrosive enough to require this warning sign on its containers.
questions.solution_hindi: सोडियम हाइड्रॉक्साइड (NaOH) एक अत्यंत संक्षारक पदार्थ है जो त्वचा और आँखों को गंभीर क्षति पहुँचा सकता है। इसलिए इसके पात्रों पर संक्षारक चेतावनी चिह्न लगाना अनिवार्य है।

questions.text: दो भिन्न मिश्रातुओं को प्राप्त करने के लिए गलित कॉपर (प्राथमिक धातु) में निश्चित अनुपात में जिंक और टिन को पृथक-पृथक विलीन किया गया है। इनसे क्रमशः जो दो भिन्न मिश्रातु बनते हैं, उन्हें कहते हैं:
questions.text_english: Two metals zinc and tin are dissolved separately in definite proportions in molten copper (the primary metal) to obtain two different alloys respectively known as:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Brass and Bronze. When zinc is dissolved in molten copper in a definite proportion, the alloy formed is Brass (Cu + Zn). When tin is dissolved in molten copper in a definite proportion, the alloy formed is Bronze (Cu + Sn). Solder is an alloy of lead and tin, not copper. Therefore options A, B, and D are incorrect. The sequence zinc → Brass and tin → Bronze makes option C the correct answer.
questions.solution_hindi: तांबे (कॉपर) में जिंक मिलाने पर पीतल (Brass) और टिन मिलाने पर ब्रान्ज (Bronze) बनता है। सोल्डर लेड और टिन का मिश्रातु है, कॉपर का नहीं।

questions.text: थर्मिट वेल्डिंग में ऐलुमिनियम चूर्ण का उपयोग किया जाता है क्योंकि:
questions.text_english: Aluminium powder is used in thermit welding because:

options.A: ऐलुमिनियम की आयरन के साथ अभिक्रिया अत्यधिक ऊष्माक्षेपी है।
options.B: ऐलुमिनियम को जब आयरन (III) ऑक्साइड के साथ गर्म किया जाता है, तो गलित आयरन प्राप्त होता है।
options.C: ऐलुमिनियम को जब आयरन (III) ऑक्साइड के साथ गर्म किया जाता है, तो गलित ऐलुमिनियम ऑक्साइड प्राप्त होता है जो रेल की पटरियों को जोड़ता है।
options.D: ऐलुमिनियम का गलनांक आयरन के गलनांक से कम है तथा गर्म करने पर ऐलुमिनियम और आयरन का गलित मिश्रातु बनता है जो रेल की पटरियों को जोड़ता है।

options_english.A: Its reaction with iron is highly exothermic.
options_english.B: When it is heated with iron (III) oxide, molten iron is obtained.
options_english.C: When it is heated with iron (III) oxide, molten aluminium oxide is obtained to join railway tracks.
options_english.D: Its melting point is low as compared to iron and a molten alloy of iron and aluminium is formed on heating which is used to join railway tracks.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). In thermit welding, aluminium powder reacts with iron (III) oxide (Fe₂O₃) in a displacement reaction: 2Al + Fe₂O₃ → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe. This produces molten iron at very high temperature, which is used to join railway tracks. Option A is incomplete as it does not specify the role of the product. Option C is wrong because it says molten aluminium oxide joins the tracks, whereas it is actually the molten iron. Option D is incorrect as no alloy is formed.
questions.solution_hindi: थर्मिट वेल्डिंग में एलुमिनियम, Fe₂O₃ से अभिक्रिया करके गलित आयरन उत्पन्न करता है: 2Al + Fe₂O₃ → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe। यह गलित आयरन रेल की पटरियों को जोड़ने के काम आता है।

questions.text: मानव हृदय के प्रकार्य के बारे में निम्नलिखित कथनों में से सही विकल्प चुनिए:
questions.text_english: Select the correct option from the following statements about the functioning of the human heart.

options.A: दायाँ अलिन्द शरीर के विभिन्न भागों से विऑक्सीजनित रुधिर ग्रहण करके उसे फुफ्फुसीय शिराओं में भेजता है।
options.B: बायाँ अलिन्द ऑक्सीजनित रुधिर को दाएँ निलय को भेजता है जो उसे शरीर के विभिन्न भागों को पम्प कर देता है।
options.C: दायाँ अलिन्द शरीर से विऑक्सीजनित रुधिर ग्रहण करके उसे दाएँ निलय को भेज देता है।
options.D: बायाँ अलिन्द फुफ्फुसीय धमनियों से ऑक्सीजनित रुधिर ग्रहण करके उसे बाएँ निलय को भेज देता है।

options_english.A: Right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from different parts of the body and sends it to pulmonary veins.
options_english.B: Left atrium sends oxygenated blood to right ventricle which pumps it to different parts of the body.
options_english.C: Right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the body and sends it to the right ventricle.
options_english.D: Left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the pulmonary arteries and sends it to the left ventricle.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from all parts of the body through the venae cavae and pumps it into the right ventricle, which then sends it to the lungs via the pulmonary artery. Option A is wrong because the right atrium sends blood to the pulmonary artery, not pulmonary veins. Option B is wrong because oxygenated blood goes from the left atrium to the left ventricle, not to the right. Option D is wrong because oxygenated blood comes from the pulmonary veins, not pulmonary arteries, to the left atrium.
questions.solution_hindi: दायाँ अलिन्द शरीर से विऑक्सीजनित रुधिर ग्रहण करता है और उसे दाएँ निलय को भेजता है। बायाँ अलिन्द फुफ्फुसीय शिराओं से ऑक्सीजनित रुधिर ग्रहण करता है।

questions.text: दिए गए आरेख A और B का प्रेक्षण कीजिए। जब किसी छुई-मुई (सुग्राही) पौधे को स्पर्श किया जाता है, तो उसकी पत्तियाँ मुड़ जाती हैं। इसका कारण है:
questions.text_english: Observe the given figures A and B. When chhui-mui (sensitive) plant is touched, its leaves fold. This is due to:

options.C: कोशिकाओं में जल की मात्रा में परिवर्तन

options_english.C: Change in amount of water in cells

questions.image_description: Two photographs of Mimosa pudica (touch-me-not / chhui-mui plant). Figure A shows the plant with leaves open and Figure B shows the same plant with leaves folded after being touched.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Change in amount of water in cells. The touch-me-not plant (Mimosa pudica) responds to touch through a rapid movement caused by changes in turgor pressure. When touched, the cells at the base of the leaflets (pulvinus cells) lose water rapidly due to changes in osmotic pressure, causing the leaves to droop and fold. This is not a hormonal response (which is slower) nor a thermal or electromagnetic effect. This type of movement is called seismonastic movement.
questions.solution_hindi: छुई-मुई पौधे में स्पर्श होने पर पर्णवृंत के आधार की कोशिकाओं (पल्विनस) में जल की मात्रा में परिवर्तन होता है जिससे स्फीति दबाव घट जाता है और पत्तियाँ मुड़ जाती हैं। इसे सीस्मोनास्टिक गति कहते हैं।

questions.text: एक कोशिकीय मोटी रुधिर वाहिकाओं को क्या कहते हैं?
questions.text_english: One-cell thick blood vessels are known as:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Capillaries. Capillaries are the smallest and thinnest blood vessels in the body, with walls that are only one cell thick. This thin wall allows easy exchange of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nutrients and waste products between the blood and surrounding tissues. Arteries and veins have thick, multi-layered walls. Alveoli are tiny air sacs in the lungs, not blood vessels.
questions.solution_hindi: केशिकाएँ (Capillaries) एक कोशिका मोटी दीवार वाली रुधिर वाहिकाएँ होती हैं। इनकी पतली दीवार के कारण रक्त और ऊतकों के बीच पदार्थों का आदान-प्रदान आसानी से होता है।

questions.text: किसी पुष्पी पादप के मादा जनन तंत्र में दिए गए भागों का व्यवस्था के अनुसार निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा सही अनुक्रम है?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is the correct sequence of parts of female reproductive system of flowering plants in terms of their placement?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Stigma, style, ovary, ovule. The female reproductive organ of a flower is called the pistil or carpel. Starting from the top: the Stigma is the sticky tip that receives pollen grains. Below it is the Style, which is the elongated tube connecting stigma to the ovary. The Ovary is the swollen base that contains the Ovules, which develop into seeds after fertilization. This top-to-bottom arrangement makes option D the correct sequence.
questions.solution_hindi: पुष्पी पादप के मादा जनन अंग (स्त्रीकेसर) में ऊपर से नीचे का क्रम इस प्रकार है: वर्तिकाग्र (Stigma) → वर्तिका (Style) → अंडाशय (Ovary) → बीजाण्ड (Ovule)।
questions.topic: Female Reproductive System of Flowering Plants

questions.text: किसी कोशिका विभाजन में गुणसूत्रों की संख्या आधी हो गई है। इस प्रकार के कोशिका विभाजन का प्रेक्षण कहाँ किया जाता है?
questions.text_english: The number of chromosomes in a cell division is halved. This kind of cell division is observed in:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Ovary and testis both. The cell division in which the number of chromosomes is halved is called meiosis or reduction division. Meiosis occurs in the reproductive organs — in the testis (where sperm cells are formed) and in the ovary (where egg cells are formed). This halving of chromosomes ensures that when fertilization occurs, the resulting zygote has the normal diploid chromosome number. Options A and B are partially correct but incomplete. Option D is wrong as mitosis (not meiosis) occurs in all body cells.
questions.solution_hindi: जिस कोशिका विभाजन में गुणसूत्रों की संख्या आधी हो जाती है, उसे अर्धसूत्री विभाजन (Meiosis) कहते हैं। यह वृषण और अंडाशय दोनों में होता है, जहाँ क्रमशः शुक्राणु और अण्डाणु बनते हैं।

questions.text: कोई विद्युत बल्ब 220 V की विद्युत आपूर्ति से संयोजित है। यदि यह बल्ब आपूर्ति से 500 mA धारा लेता है, तो इस बल्ब की शक्ति है:
questions.text_english: An electric bulb is connected to a power supply of 220 V. If the current drawn by the bulb from the supply is 500 mA, the power of the bulb is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) 110 W. Using the formula P = V × I, where V = 220 V and I = 500 mA = 0.5 A. Therefore P = 220 × 0.5 = 110 W. Option A (11 W) would result from using 0.05 A instead of 0.5 A. Option C (220 W) would require a current of 1 A. Option D (1100 W) would require a current of 5 A. The unit conversion of mA to A is crucial here: 500 mA = 0.5 A.

questions.text: 12 Ω के चार सर्वसम प्रतिरोधक आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार श्रेणीक्रम में संयोजित होकर वर्ग ABCD बनाते हैं। इस नेटवर्क के दो बिन्दुओं 1 और 2 के बीच प्रतिरोध है:
questions.text_english: Four identical resistors of 12 Ω each are connected in series to form a square ABCD as shown in the figure. The resistance of the network between the two points 1 and 2 is:
questions.image_description: A circuit diagram showing four 12 Ω resistors connected in series forming a square ABCD. Point 1 is at the top-left (at A) and point 2 is at the top-right (at B). Resistors are along each side: A-B (top), B-D (right), D-C (bottom), C-A (left).
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 6 Ω. Points 1 and 2 are at vertices A and B respectively. From point 1 (A) to point 2 (B), there are two paths: Path 1 (direct, through top resistor A-B): resistance = 12 Ω. Path 2 (through A-C-D-B, i.e., three resistors): resistance = 12 + 12 + 12 = 36 Ω. These two paths are in parallel between points 1 and 2. Equivalent resistance = (12 × 36)/(12 + 36) = 432/48 = 9 Ω. Wait — re-checking: Path 1 = AB = 12 Ω, Path 2 = A→C→D→B = 36 Ω. Parallel combination = (12 × 36)/(12 + 36) = 432/48 = 9 Ω. So the correct answer is (C) 9 Ω.

questions.text: मानव नेत्र का वह भाग कौन-सा है जो अभिनेत्र लेंस की वक्रता में कुछ सीमा तक रूपान्तरण कर सकता है?
questions.text_english: The part of the human eye which can modify the curvature of the eye lens to some extent is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Ciliary muscles. The ciliary muscles are ring-like muscles attached to the eye lens. They control the shape and curvature of the crystalline lens, allowing the eye to focus on objects at different distances — a process called accommodation. When ciliary muscles contract, the lens becomes more convex (for near vision); when they relax, the lens becomes flatter (for distant vision). The pupil controls light entry, the cornea is a fixed transparent layer, and aqueous humour is a fluid that maintains eye pressure.
questions.solution_hindi: पक्ष्माभी पेशियाँ (Ciliary muscles) नेत्र लेंस की वक्रता को नियंत्रित करती हैं। इनके संकुचन और शिथिलन से लेंस की फोकस दूरी बदलती है जिससे दूर और पास की वस्तुएँ स्पष्ट दिखती हैं। इस प्रक्रिया को समंजन (Accommodation) कहते हैं।
questions.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

questions.text: यदि दो माध्यमों X और Y के निरपेक्ष अपवर्तनांक क्रमशः 6/5 और 4/3 हैं, तो X के सापेक्ष Y का अपवर्तनांक होगा:
questions.text_english: If the absolute refractive indices of two media X and Y are 6/5 and 4/3 respectively, then the refractive index of Y with respect to X will be:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) 10/9. The refractive index of Y with respect to X is calculated as: ₓnᵧ = nᵧ / nₓ, where nₓ = 6/5 and nᵧ = 4/3. Therefore ₓnᵧ = (4/3) ÷ (6/5) = (4/3) × (5/6) = 20/18 = 10/9. Option B (9/10) would be the refractive index of X with respect to Y. Options C and D are incorrect calculations. The formula requires dividing the refractive index of Y by that of X.

questions.text: कोई बिम्ब किसी अवतल दर्पण के ध्रुव से 30 cm दूरी पर स्थित है। यदि इस बिम्ब का वास्तविक और उल्टा प्रतिबिम्ब इस दर्पण के सामने 60 cm दूरी पर बनता है, तो दर्पण की फोकस दूरी है:
questions.text_english: An object is placed at a distance of 30 cm from the pole of a concave mirror. If its real and inverted image is formed at 60 cm in front of the mirror, the focal length of the mirror is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) –20 cm. Using the mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u. For a concave mirror, using sign convention: u = –30 cm (object in front), v = –60 cm (real image in front of mirror). 1/f = 1/(–60) + 1/(–30) = –1/60 – 2/60 = –3/60 = –1/20. Therefore f = –20 cm. The negative sign confirms it is a concave mirror. Option A (–15 cm) is incorrect as the calculation gives –20 cm. Options C and D have positive values which would indicate a convex mirror.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से सभी अजैव-निम्नीकरणीय पदार्थों के समूह को पहचानिए।
questions.text_english: Identify from the following a group containing all non-biodegradable substances.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) DDT, Polyester, Glass. All three are non-biodegradable substances: DDT is a persistent pesticide that does not decompose naturally; Polyester is a synthetic polymer that resists microbial breakdown; Glass is an inorganic material that does not decompose. Option A is incorrect because leather is biodegradable. Option B is incorrect because cotton and wood are both biodegradable. Option D is incorrect because silk and wool are natural animal fibres and are biodegradable.
questions.solution_hindi: DDT, पॉलिएस्टर और काँच — तीनों अजैव-निम्नीकरणीय पदार्थ हैं। चमड़ा, कपास, लकड़ी, रेशम और ऊन जैव-निम्नीकरणीय हैं।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): तन्यता वह गुण है जिसके कारण कॉपर का उपयोग खाना/भोजन पकाने के बर्तन बनाने में किया जा सकता है। 
कारण (R): कॉपर ऐसी धातु है जो तन्य के साथ-साथ आघातवध्य भी है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Ductility is that property of metals which enables copper to be used in making cooking utensils.
Reason (R): Copper is a metal which is ductile as well as malleable.
questions.instruction_line: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों में से उचित विकल्प चुनिए।

questions.solution: (a) The reaction that takes place is a Displacement Reaction. Copper, being more reactive than silver, displaces silver from silver nitrate solution. On passing electric current, pure silver deposits at the cathode.

questions.text_english: What are micelles? Draw the structure.

key_points: Micelle is a cluster/aggregate formed by soap molecules in water
Structure: hydrophilic head points outward towards water, hydrophobic tail points inward

questions.image_description: A circular diagram showing a micelle structure. The outer surface has hydrophilic (water-loving) heads of soap molecules pointing outward, and the inner core has the hydrophobic (water-fearing) hydrocarbon tails pointing inward, with a dirt/grease particle trapped in the centre.
questions.solution: When soap is dissolved in water, the soap molecules arrange themselves in a spherical cluster called a micelle. In a micelle, the hydrophilic (water-loving) ionic end of each soap molecule points outward towards the water, while the hydrophobic (water-repelling) hydrocarbon tail points inward away from water. The dirt or grease particles get trapped inside the micelle in the hydrophobic core. When water is rinsed, the entire micelle — along with the dirt — gets washed away. The structure of a micelle is a sphere with outward-facing heads and inward-facing tails surrounding a dirt particle in the centre.

questions.solution: The fore-brain is the most complex and developed part of the human brain. It controls thinking, memory, and voluntary actions. When a person makes a shopping list, the fore-brain recalls what items are needed from memory, thinks about the requirements, makes decisions about what to purchase, and coordinates voluntary actions like holding a pen and writing. The cerebrum (part of fore-brain) integrates sensory information and directs the hand to write the list. It also helps in reasoning — for example, deciding quantities or budget — making it essential for this planned, conscious activity.

questions.solution: The functions of seed parts are: (i) Seed coat (Testa) — It protects the seed from physical damage, pathogens, and loss of water, keeping the embryo safe until germination conditions are favourable. (ii) Cotyledon — It stores food (in the form of starch, proteins, and fats) which nourishes the embryo during germination before the seedling can make its own food. (iii) Radicle — It is the embryonic root that germinates first and develops into the complete root system, anchoring the plant in the soil and absorbing water. (iv) Plumule — It is the embryonic shoot that develops into the aerial stem and leaves of the new plant.

(a) Out of the two lenses, one concave and the other convex, state which one will diverge a parallel beam of light falling on it. Draw a ray diagram to show the principal focus of the lens.

OR

(b) A ray of light after refraction from a convex lens emerges parallel to its principal axis.
(i) Draw a labelled ray diagram to show it.
(ii) In this case, the incident ray before refraction from the lens passes through a point on its principal axis. Name the point.

key_points: Concave lens diverges a parallel beam of light
The refracted rays appear to diverge from the principal focus F on the same side as the incident light (virtual focus)

questions.image_description: Ray diagram of a concave lens showing parallel rays of light falling on it and diverging after refraction. The diverged rays, when extended backward, appear to meet at the principal focus F on the same side as the incident light. The optical centre O and principal axis are labelled.
questions.solution: A concave lens diverges a parallel beam of light falling on it. When parallel rays of light are incident on a concave lens, after refraction they spread apart (diverge). When these diverged rays are extended backwards, they appear to meet at a point on the same side as the incident light. This point is called the principal focus (F) of the concave lens. It is a virtual focus because the refracted rays do not actually pass through it. The distance from the optical centre O to F is the focal length of the concave lens, which is always negative by sign convention.

questions.text_english: How and why is an electric fuse used in an electric circuit? Briefly describe its function.

key_points: Fuse is used to protect electrical circuits from overloading and short circuits
It is made of a thin wire of low melting point material (like tin-lead alloy) connected in series in the circuit

questions.solution: A fuse is a safety device used in electric circuits to protect appliances and wiring from damage caused by excessive current. It is made of a thin wire of a material with low melting point (such as tin-lead alloy) and is connected in series with the circuit. When the current in the circuit exceeds the rated value due to overloading or a short circuit, the fuse wire heats up rapidly and melts, breaking the circuit and stopping the current flow. This prevents damage to the connected appliances and reduces the risk of fire. The fuse must be replaced after it melts to restore the circuit.

(a) (i) Define the term decomposition reaction. Write one chemical equation each for decomposition reaction where energy is supplied in the form of heat, light or electricity.

Composting is exothermic because energy is released during breakdown of organic matter

questions.solution: A decomposition reaction is one in which a single reactant breaks down into two or more simpler products when energy is supplied. Examples: (i) Thermal decomposition: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ (calcium carbonate decomposes on heating to form calcium oxide and carbon dioxide). (ii) Photodecomposition: 2AgBr → 2Ag + Br₂ (silver bromide decomposes in sunlight to form silver and bromine). (iii) Electrolytic decomposition: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂ (water decomposes on passing electric current to form hydrogen and oxygen). Decomposition of vegetable matter into compost is exothermic because micro-organisms break down complex organic molecules and in doing so release energy in the form of heat. This is why compost pits feel warm during the process.

key_points: X gives blue colour: basic/alkaline nature, pH 8–14
Y gives orange colour: acidic nature, pH 1–6
A is the metal because metals form basic oxides which dissolve in water to give alkaline solutions

questions.solution: (a) Solution X gives light blue colour to the pH paper, which indicates that X is basic (alkaline) in nature with pH in the range of 8 to 14. Solution Y gives orange colour to the pH paper, which indicates that Y is acidic in nature with pH in the range of 1 to 6. (b) A is the metal. Justification: When metals burn in air, they form metal oxides. Metal oxides are basic in nature and when dissolved in water, they form alkaline solutions. B is a non-metal because its fumes dissolve in water to form an acidic solution (pH < 7), which is characteristic of non-metallic oxides.

key_points: Hormone: chemical messenger secreted by endocrine glands, transported in blood to target organs
Feedback mechanism: when blood sugar rises, more insulin is secreted; when it falls, less is secreted — this maintains balance

questions.solution: (a) Hormones are chemical messengers secreted by endocrine glands directly into the blood. They are secreted in very small quantities but have powerful effects on specific target organs. They regulate various physiological processes and help in coordination. (b) The feedback mechanism ensures that hormones are secreted in precise amounts. For example, when blood glucose levels rise after eating, the pancreas secretes more insulin. Insulin helps body cells absorb glucose, thus lowering blood sugar back to normal. When blood glucose falls to the normal level, the signal to secrete insulin stops. This self-regulating loop is the feedback mechanism that maintains hormonal balance in the body.

questions.text_english:
A pure pea plant bearing terminal flowers was cross-pollinated with a pure plant having axillary flowers. In F₁ generation, plants with axial flowers only were obtained. F₁ generation plants are self-pollinated and F₂ generation is obtained.
(a) Work out the pattern of inheritance in this case.
(b) What will be the ratio of plants obtained in F₂ generation?

key_points: Axial flower is dominant (A), terminal flower is recessive (a)
Cross: AA × aa → F1: all Aa (axial)
F1 × F1: Aa × Aa → F2: 1AA : 2Aa : 1aa = 3 axial : 1 terminal

questions.solution: (a) Since only axial-flowered plants appeared in F₁, axial position is the dominant trait and terminal position is the recessive trait. Let A = axial (dominant), a = terminal (recessive). Parental cross: AA (axial) × aa (terminal) → F₁: all Aa (axial). F₁ self-pollination: Aa × Aa → F₂: AA : Aa : aa = 1 : 2 : 1. (b) In F₂ generation, the phenotypic ratio is 3 axial-flowered plants : 1 terminal-flowered plant, i.e., a ratio of 3:1. This demonstrates Mendel's Law of Segregation, where the recessive trait that disappears in F₁ reappears in F₂ in 1/4 of the offspring.
questions.solution_hindi: (क) अक्षीय पुष्प प्रभावी (A) और अन्त्य पुष्प अप्रभावी (a) है। AA × aa → F₁ सभी Aa (अक्षीय)। Aa × Aa → F₂: 1AA : 2Aa : 1aa। (ख) F₂ में अनुपात: 3 अक्षीय : 1 अन्त्य = 3:1।

questions.text_english: A convex mirror used for rear view on an automobile has a focal length of 15 m. If a 3 m high bus is located at 60 m from the mirror, use mirror formula to determine the position and size of the image of the bus as seen in the mirror.

key_points: v = +12 m (image formed 12 m behind the mirror)
Size of image = 0.6 m (magnification = +1/5)

questions.solution: For a convex mirror, using sign convention: f = +15 m, u = –60 m. Using mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u. 1/15 = 1/v + 1/(–60). 1/v = 1/15 + 1/60 = 4/60 + 1/60 = 5/60 = 1/12. Therefore v = +12 m. The image is formed 12 m behind the mirror (virtual, erect). Magnification m = –v/u = –(+12)/(–60) = 12/60 = +1/5. Size of image = m × object size = (1/5) × 3 = 0.6 m. The image of the bus is 0.6 m tall, virtual, and erect, located 12 m behind the mirror.

questions.text_english: Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in (i) series, and (ii) parallel. Draw the arrangements of the resistors and find the equivalent resistance of each arrangement.

key_points: (i) Series: Rs = 2 + 3 + 6 = 11 Ω
(ii) Parallel: 1/Rp = 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = 1, so Rp = 1 Ω

questions.image_description: Two circuit diagrams. First diagram shows three resistors (2Ω, 3Ω, 6Ω) connected end to end in series with a battery. Second diagram shows the same three resistors connected in parallel (all connected between the same two points) with a battery.
questions.solution: (i) Series connection: When resistors are connected in series, the equivalent resistance is the sum of all resistances. Rs = R₁ + R₂ + R₃ = 2 + 3 + 6 = 11 Ω. (ii) Parallel connection: When resistors are connected in parallel, 1/Rp = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃ = 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = 3/6 + 2/6 + 1/6 = 6/6 = 1. Therefore Rp = 1 Ω. In parallel, the equivalent resistance is always less than the smallest individual resistance (here 2 Ω). In series, it is always greater than the largest individual resistance.

questions.text_english: Some harmful chemicals get accumulated in human bodies through the food chain. Name this phenomenon. Explain the reason of maximum concentration of these chemicals found in our bodies.

key_points: Phenomenon: Biological Magnification (Bio-magnification)
Humans are at the top of food chains so they accumulate the highest concentration of harmful chemicals

questions.solution: This phenomenon is called Biological Magnification or Bio-magnification. It refers to the progressive increase in the concentration of harmful chemicals (such as pesticides like DDT) at each successive trophic level of a food chain. Humans have the maximum concentration of these chemicals in their bodies because humans occupy the highest trophic level (top of the food chain). At each level, the organisms consume large amounts of organisms from the level below and the non-biodegradable chemicals from all of them accumulate in their body tissues. Since these chemicals cannot be broken down and are not excreted, they keep accumulating. By the time it reaches humans, the concentration becomes several times higher than at the producer level.
questions.solution_hindi: इस परिघटना को जैव-आवर्धन (Biological Magnification) कहते हैं। मनुष्य खाद्य श्रृंखला में सर्वोच्च स्तर पर होता है और नीचे के सभी जीवों के अजैव-निम्नीकरणीय रसायन उसके शरीर में संग्रहित हो जाते हैं। इसलिए मनुष्य में इनकी सांद्रता अधिकतम होती है।

(a) The given figure shows the current passing through the straight conductor XY.
(i) Copy the diagram and draw the magnetic field lines when current flows from conductor X to Y.
(ii) Name and state the rule used in determining the direction of the magnetic field lines in the situation given above.
(iii) State Fleming's left hand rule. Using this rule, determine the direction of force applied on an electron entering a uniform magnetic field as shown in the figure.

OR

(b)(i) Define the term solenoid. Draw the pattern of the magnetic field lines in and around a current carrying straight solenoid. Mark on the pattern the (i) direction of current, (ii) direction of field lines near the ends of the solenoid, and (iii) region where the magnetic field is uniform.
(ii) How would you make an electromagnet using a current carrying solenoid?

key_points: Magnetic field lines form concentric circles around the conductor; direction found by Right-Hand Thumb Rule
Right-Hand Thumb Rule: if thumb points in direction of current, fingers curl in direction of field
Fleming's Left Hand Rule: stretch thumb, index and middle finger mutually perpendicular; index = B, middle = I (conventional), thumb = Force
Electron moves to right, B is to the right; conventional current is opposite to electron motion; force is downward (into the page)

questions.image_description: Circuit diagram showing straight conductor XY connected to a battery through a variable resistance and switch K. Also a separate diagram showing an electron 'e' moving horizontally to the right entering a uniform magnetic field directed horizontally to the right (arrows pointing right). The electron enters from below with an upward velocity component.
questions.solution:
(i) When current flows from X to Y (downward through the conductor), the magnetic field lines form concentric circles around the conductor. The direction of the circles can be found using the Right-Hand Thumb Rule.

(ii) Right-Hand Thumb Rule (Maxwell's Corkscrew Rule): If the thumb of the right hand is held in the direction of the conventional current through a conductor, then the fingers curled around the conductor point in the direction of the magnetic field lines. For current flowing from X to Y (downward), the field lines form anticlockwise circles when viewed from below.

(iii) Fleming's Left Hand Rule: Stretch the thumb, index finger and middle finger of the left hand mutually perpendicular to each other. If the index finger points in the direction of the magnetic field (B) and the middle finger points in the direction of conventional current (I), then the thumb points in the direction of the force (F) on the conductor. For the electron entering the magnetic field: the electron moves to the right, so conventional current is to the left. Magnetic field (B) is to the right. Using Fleming's Left Hand Rule with current to the left and B to the right, the force on the conventional current would be downward (into the page). Since the electron has negative charge, the actual force on the electron is upward (out of the page).

(ii) Write the method of converting an unsaturated hydrocarbon into a saturated hydrocarbon. Name the industry where this reaction is commonly used.

key_points: X is Acetic acid (CH₃COOH / Ethanoic acid)

Esterification reaction: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH → CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O

questions.solution:
(i) Compound X is Acetic acid (Ethanoic acid), chemical formula CH₃COOH. It has two carbon atoms, turns blue litmus red (acidic), and its 5–8% solution (vinegar) is widely used as a food preservative. Structure: CH₃–COOH (with a carboxyl group –COOH attached to a methyl group CH₃–).

(ii) Acetic acid is a weak acid and has a higher pH value compared to a mineral acid (like HCl or H₂SO₄) of the same concentration. Mineral acids are strong acids that completely ionise in water (very low pH, around 1–2), whereas acetic acid is partially ionised (pH around 3–4). Both are acidic (pH < 7) but mineral acids are much stronger.

(iii) The reaction between acetic acid and alcohol is called Esterification. Chemical equation: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O (in presence of acid catalyst H₂SO₄). The product CH₃COOC₂H₅ is ethyl ethanoate (ethyl acetate), a sweet-smelling ester used in perfumes.

(iv) When sodium carbonate is added to acetic acid: 2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂↑. The colourless CO₂ gas turns lime water milky. The salt formed is Sodium acetate (Sodium ethanoate), CH₃COONa.

(iii) पाचित भोजन को अवशोषित करने के लिए क्षुदांत्र की अभिकल्पना किस प्रकार की गई है?
questions.text_english:
(a)(i) "The length of the small intestine in various animals depends on the food they eat." Justify the statement.
(ii) Discuss the role of the pancreas and bile juice in the digestion of food in human beings.
(iii) How is the small intestine designed to absorb digested food?

OR

(b)(i) State the role of rings of cartilage present in the throat.
(ii) Discuss the role of the ribs and diaphragm when air is taken in during the breathing cycle.
(iii) Why do we get muscle cramps during heavy exercise? Explain.

key_points: Herbivores have longer intestine (for cellulose digestion); carnivores have shorter intestine
Pancreas secretes pancreatic juice (amylase, lipase, trypsin); bile emulsifies fats
Small intestine has villi and microvilli that increase surface area for absorption

questions.solution:
(i) The length of the small intestine depends on the diet of the animal. Herbivores (plant-eating animals like cows) have a very long small intestine because plant matter (cellulose) is difficult to digest and requires a longer time and more surface area for breakdown. Carnivores (meat-eating animals like tigers) have a shorter small intestine because proteins in meat are relatively easier to digest. Omnivores like humans have an intermediate length.

(ii) The pancreas secretes pancreatic juice which contains three important enzymes: pancreatic amylase (breaks down starch into sugars), trypsin (breaks down proteins into amino acids), and lipase (breaks down emulsified fats into fatty acids and glycerol). Bile juice, secreted by the liver and stored in the gall bladder, does not contain enzymes but it emulsifies fats — breaking large fat droplets into smaller ones — which increases the surface area for lipase to act on.

(iii) The small intestine is specially designed for maximum absorption. Its inner wall has numerous finger-like projections called villi (singular: villus), which greatly increase the surface area available for absorption. Each villus contains a network of blood capillaries and a lymph vessel (lacteal). The digested food — glucose, amino acids, fatty acids — is absorbed through the villi into the blood and lymph for transport to all body cells.
questions.solution_hindi: (i) शाकाहारी जन्तुओं की क्षुदांत्र लंबी होती है (सेल्युलोज पाचन हेतु), मांसाहारी की छोटी होती है। (ii) अग्न्याशय एमाइलेज, ट्रिप्सिन और लाइपेज स्रावित करता है। पित्त रस वसाओं का पायसीकरण करता है। (iii) क्षुदांत्र की आंतरिक दीवार पर रसांकुर (Villi) होते हैं जो अवशोषण क्षेत्रफल बढ़ाते हैं।

questions.text: किसी लड़की के जन्म के समय ही उसके अंडाशय में हजारों अपरिपक्व अंड होते हैं। यौवनारम्भ में, इनमें से कुछ परिपक्व होने लगते हैं। दोनों अंडाशयों में से एक अंडाशय द्वारा प्रतिमाह एक परिपक्व अंड मोचित होता है। दो अंडवाहिकाएँ संयुक्त होकर एक लचीली थैलेनुमा संरचना का निर्माण करती हैं जिसे गर्भाशय कहते हैं।
questions.text_english: When a girl is born, the ovaries already contain thousands of immature eggs. On reaching puberty, some of these start maturing. One matured egg is released every month by one of the ovaries. The two oviducts unite into an elastic bag-like structure known as uterus.

sub_questions.text: मानव महिला में निषेचन का स्थल लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write the site of fertilization in human female.

key_points: Fallopian tube (oviduct)

sub_questions.solution: In the human female, fertilization takes place in the Fallopian tube (oviduct). The egg, after being released from the ovary, travels into the fallopian tube where it meets the sperm and fertilization occurs, forming a zygote.

sub_questions.text: गर्भाशय किस प्रकार स्वयं को विकसित होते भ्रूण की प्राप्ति और उसके पोषण के लिए तैयार करता है? व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: How does the uterus prepare itself to receive and nurture the growing embryo? Explain.

key_points: Uterine lining (endometrium) thickens with blood supply to receive and nourish the embryo

sub_questions.solution: When the egg is released each month, the uterus prepares itself to receive a fertilized egg by developing a thick, spongy lining of blood and mucus called the endometrium. This lining is rich in blood vessels and provides nourishment to the developing embryo. Once the fertilized egg (blastocyst) reaches the uterus, it implants into this thickened lining and continues to develop, receiving nutrients and oxygen through the uterine wall and later through the placenta.

sub_questions.text: क्या होता है जब अंड का निषेचन नहीं होता है?
sub_questions.text_english: What happens when the egg is not fertilized?

key_points: Egg degenerates and is reabsorbed
Uterine lining breaks down and is shed — this is menstruation

sub_questions.solution: When the egg is not fertilized, the prepared uterine lining (endometrium) is no longer needed. The thickened lining, along with the unfertilized egg and blood vessels, breaks down and is shed from the body through the vagina. This process is called menstruation and occurs approximately every 28 days. After menstruation, the uterine lining begins to build up again for the next cycle, preparing for a possible fertilization in the next month.

questions.text: किसी व्यक्ति ने सूर्य के श्वेत प्रकाश के महीन पुंज को किसी लघुद्वारक से किसी अँधेरे कमरे में प्रवेश कराया तथा प्रकाश पुंज के पथ में किसी काँच के प्रिज़्म को इस प्रकार रखा गया कि प्रकाश पुंज आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार प्रिज़्म के फलक AB पर आपतन करे। किसी पर्दे S को प्रिज़्म के दूसरी ओर, AC के सामने रखा गया। प्रिज़्म को धीरे-धीरे घुमाने पर, पर्दे पर वर्णों की आकर्षक पट्टी प्राप्त होती है। यह सूर्य के प्रकाश का स्पेक्ट्रम है।
questions.text_english: A person allowed a narrow beam of white light from the sun to enter a dark room through a small aperture and placed a glass prism in its path in such a manner that the beam falls on the face AB of the prism as shown in the figure. A screen S is placed on the other side of the prism, facing AC. On turning the prism slowly, a beautiful band of colours is obtained on the screen. It is the spectrum of sunlight.

sub_questions.text: उस परिघटना का नाम लिखिए जिसके कारण कोई प्रिज़्म आपतित श्वेत प्रकाश को वर्णों की पट्टी में विभक्त कर देता है।
sub_questions.text_english: Name the phenomenon due to which a prism splits the incident white light into a band of colours.

key_points: Dispersion of light

sub_questions.solution: The phenomenon due to which a prism splits white light into a band of colours is called Dispersion of Light. When white light enters a glass prism, each colour (wavelength) bends by a different amount, causing them to separate and produce a spectrum on the screen.

sub_questions.text: उपयुक्त प्रकरण में सात वर्णों की पट्टी प्राप्त होने का कारण लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: State the reason of getting a band of seven colours in the above case.

key_points: White light is composed of seven colours each with different wavelength
Each colour has a different refractive index in glass and bends by a different amount

sub_questions.solution: A band of seven colours (VIBGYOR) is obtained because white light is actually a mixture of seven different colours — violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, and red. Each colour has a different wavelength and therefore a different speed in glass, giving it a different refractive index. When white light enters the prism, each colour bends by a different angle (violet bends the most and red the least), causing them to separate and form a rainbow-coloured band called spectrum.

sub_questions.text: नामांकित किरण आरेख की सहायता से, श्वेत प्रकाश के स्पेक्ट्रम का पुनर्योजन दर्शाने की प्रायोगिक व्यवस्था की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain with the help of a labelled ray diagram, an experimental arrangement to show the recombination of the spectrum of white light.

key_points: Two identical prisms placed in inverted positions (base-to-base)
First prism disperses white light; second prism recombines the colours back to white light

sub_questions.solution: To show the recombination of spectrum back into white light, two identical glass prisms are placed in inverted positions (with their bases facing each other). White light is passed through the first prism which disperses it into its seven constituent colours (VIBGYOR). The dispersed coloured beams then enter the second prism, which is placed in an inverted position with respect to the first. The second prism recombines all the colours by refracting them in the opposite direction. When the recombined beam falls on a screen, white light is obtained, proving that white light is made up of seven colours and that dispersion is a reversible process.

questions.text: अम्ल-क्षारक सूचकों का उपयोग अम्ल और क्षारक में विभेदन करने के लिए किया जा सकता है। सार्वत्रिक सूचक, जो अनेक सूचकों का मिश्रण है, अम्लों और क्षारकों की विभिन्न सांद्रताओं के लिए विभिन्न रंग दर्शाता है, जिसके द्वारा pH स्केल, जो 0–14 तक है, पर उनके pH को सूचित करता है। pH पत्र द्वारा किसी विलयन का pH मापा जाता है जो सार्वत्रिक सूचक अंतर्भारित पेपर होता है।
questions.text_english: Acid-base indicators can be used to distinguish between an acid and a base. Universal indicator, a mixture of several indicators, shows different colours at different concentrations of acids and bases, thereby indicating their pH on the pH scale of 0–14. The pH of a solution is measured by pH paper, which is a paper impregnated with a universal indicator.

sub_questions.text: विलयन P कोई प्रबल अम्ल है जबकि विलयन Q कोई प्रबल क्षारक है। pH स्केल पर आप इन विलयनों P और Q को कहाँ रखेंगे?
sub_questions.text_english: Solution P is a strong acid while solution Q is a strong base. On the pH scale, where would you place the solutions P and Q?

key_points: P (strong acid) near 0–2; Q (strong base) near 12–14

sub_questions.solution: Solution P, being a strong acid, would be placed at the lower end of the pH scale, close to 0–2. Solution Q, being a strong base, would be placed at the upper end of the pH scale, close to 12–14. Strong acids have a very high concentration of H⁺ ions (low pH) and strong bases have a very high concentration of OH⁻ ions (high pH).

sub_questions.text: किसी विलयन का pH, 7 है। उस यौगिक का नाम लिखिए जिसका उपयोग आप इस विलयन के (i) pH में वृद्धि तथा (ii) pH में कमी करने के लिए करेंगे।
sub_questions.text_english: A solution has a pH of 7. Name a compound you would use to (i) increase its pH, and (ii) decrease its pH.

key_points: (i) To increase pH: add a base such as Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)
(ii) To decrease pH: add an acid such as Hydrochloric acid (HCl)

sub_questions.solution: A solution with pH 7 is neutral. (i) To increase its pH (make it more alkaline/basic), we would add a base such as Sodium hydroxide (NaOH). Adding a base increases the OH⁻ ion concentration, which raises the pH above 7. (ii) To decrease its pH (make it more acidic), we would add an acid such as Hydrochloric acid (HCl). Adding an acid increases the H⁺ (hydronium) ion concentration, which lowers the pH below 7.

sub_questions.text: जब किसी विलयन के pH में 4 से 2 तक कमी होती है, तो उसके हाइड्रोनियम आयन की सांद्रता पर क्या प्रभाव होता है? इससे pH पत्र के रंग में होने वाले परिवर्तन का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: When the pH of a solution is decreased from 4 to 2, what effect does it produce on its hydronium ion concentration? State the colour change shown by the pH paper.

key_points: Hydronium ion concentration increases 100 times (10² = 100 fold increase)
pH paper colour changes from orange to red (more intensely red)

sub_questions.solution: When the pH of a solution decreases from 4 to 2, the hydronium ion (H₃O⁺) concentration increases. Since pH = –log[H⁺], a decrease in pH by 2 units (from 4 to 2) means the concentration of hydronium ions increases by a factor of 10² = 100 times. The solution becomes 100 times more acidic. Regarding the pH paper colour change: at pH 4, the pH paper shows an orange colour, and at pH 2 it shows a red colour (deeper/more intense red), since lower pH (more acidic) turns the universal indicator more intensely red.
